specialists_or_stages: leader (main thread): inventory, component/technology/surface matrix, staffing, deduplication, consolidation
ehs-web-api (fieldops-api, plus a web-class secondary pass over atlas-rag/ragsvc/app.py and limits.py)
ehs-web-api (settlement-worker: message consumer, ledger, idempotency, reconciliation)
ehs-supply-chain (cross-cutting: all manifests, tree-wide secret sweep)
VER-09 adversarial pass: run by each specialist against its own finished list, blind to the narrative that produced each assertion; casualties recorded in ruled_out
architecture.fell_back_and_why: Two fallbacks, both forced by the harness. (1) The plugin subagents named in references/team.md (ehs-web-api, ehs-mobile, ehs-infra-cloud, ehs-supply-chain, ehs-ai-safety, ehs-privacy-abuse, ehs-verifier) do not exist in this harness, so team.md's documented fallback path was used: every specialist ran as a general-purpose agent with the role order, scope, mode, target language, safety contract, triage rules, coverage rules and return format copied into its prompt, and with its role file and knowledge pack paths given so it loaded them itself. Because that fallback gives auditors write-capable tools, the read-only contract was imposed in the prompt instead of by the harness and verified afterwards: a SHA-256 baseline of all 60 target files was taken and re-checked at the end, and every specialist reported the tree unmodified. (2) The harness capped concurrent subagents: of seven specialists dispatched in one message, four started and three were refused. The three were staffed as slots freed, so the squad ran in two waves rather than fully in parallel; no scope was dropped. A third deviation, not a harness limit: ehs-verifier was not staffed as a separate ninth agent. VER-09 was executed by each specialist against its own list, which is weaker than the corpus's own design, since SKILL.md step 8 requires a fresh context that receives the assertion and its location and not the finder's narrative. Self-attack cannot deliver that blindness, so the adversarial stage of this run is the weakest link in it and is declared as such rather than reported as satisfied.
architecture.notes: Mode was audit (read-only) throughout; ehs-remediator was deliberately not staffed. ehs-local-app was not staffed: no CLI, desktop shell, installer, published library or local daemon exists in the tree. The corpus tools were run by every specialist and produced 1 flag in total across the whole engagement, which did not become a finding; four of the seven scopes were UNMEASURABLE for all four tools (Kotlin, XML, Gradle, SQL and Jinja are outside their reach). Both shapes those tools exist to catch — writer asymmetry and dead guards — were present in this tree and were found by hand.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection through the interpolated LIMIT/OFFSET clause in the work-order list query
ruled_out.killed_by: fieldops-api/src/routes/workorders.ts:50-51 — both operands are Number.parseInt results passed through Math.max/Math.min, so only a numeric literal can reach the template and no quote or keyword is expressible. The unbounded-page half survives as a separate finding.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection anywhere else in fieldops-api
ruled_out.killed_by: Every query uses pg positional binding with values in the parameter array; the only dynamic SQL text is sets.join(', ') at workorders.ts:147, whose members are built at lines 136-141 from a fixed set of five hardcoded column names.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection in atlas-rag
ruled_out.killed_by: All three query sites (app.py:60, :214, :232) use psycopg %s placeholders with a parameter tuple; no f-string or concatenation reaches a query. Same for retriever.py, where only source_kind becomes an extra clause and its value is bound.

ruled_out.assertion: Path traversal through storageKey into join(config.attachmentRoot, ...)
ruled_out.killed_by: fieldops-api/src/routes/attachments.ts:51 — storageKey is written only as `${randomUUID()}.bin`, the sole writer of that column in this tree, so no ../ value can reach join(). Re-open if another service writes attachments.storage_key.

ruled_out.assertion: Path traversal or header injection through the uploaded filename
ruled_out.killed_by: fieldops-api/src/routes/attachments.ts:22 — SAFE_NAME strips /, \\, CR, LF and " before the value is stored, and the name is never used to build a path; the destination is storageKey.

ruled_out.assertion: HTTP response splitting through HTTPBadRequest(reason=exc.message)
ruled_out.killed_by: jsonschema formats the offending instance through repr before building ValidationError.message, so a CR/LF in a property name or value arrives as the two-character escape, not as control characters. The disclosure half survives as a finding.

ruled_out.assertion: canWriteSite permits writing to another tenant's site
ruled_out.killed_by: fieldops-api/src/routes/workorders.ts:89 — the only call site of canWriteSite (line 92) is preceded on the same value by sameOrgSite. The PATCH gap where neither runs survives as a separate finding.

ruled_out.assertion: sameOrgSite prefix matching allows org-4 to match org-40:site-1
ruled_out.killed_by: The comparison is startsWith(`${actor.orgId}:`) — the appended colon is a delimiter no other org identifier can satisfy.

ruled_out.assertion: CSRF against the state-changing routes of either HTTP service
ruled_out.killed_by: Both services authorize exclusively through the Authorization header (auth.ts:58, app.py:72); no cookie is set or read anywhere in either component, so no ambient credential exists for a cross-site request to carry.

ruled_out.assertion: Deserialization of untrusted data in either Python service
ruled_out.killed_by: The only parsers reached are request.json()/c.req.json() and jsonschema.validate — pure data formats with no dynamic type resolution. No pickle, yaml.load, vm.runInNewContext or node-serialize appears in any component.

ruled_out.assertion: The settlement receipt — tenant, destination account, amount, balance — is disclosed to the log at INFO on every payout
ruled_out.killed_by: settlement-worker/settlement/consumer.py:122 — logging.basicConfig installs BASIC_FORMAT, which references no extra attribute, so the line that reaches the stream is 'INFO:settlement.consumer:handled'. The receipt never leaves the process this way. The inverse of this fact became the insufficient-logging finding.

ruled_out.assertion: log_escaper flags retry.py:72 as carrying attacker-influenced data into a log format string
ruled_out.killed_by: settlement-worker/settlement/retry.py:49 — count is bound from an integer initialised at :34 and incremented only at :49. It is a loop counter, never attacker-derived, and a %d conversion of an int cannot carry a control character. Tool worklist entry, not a defect.

ruled_out.assertion: A payments provider secret key is committed in two Pulumi stack config files and exported as a stack output
ruled_out.killed_by: The value carries the provider's publishable prefix and sandbox marker (redacted here after the prefix). Two in-tree confirmations independent of the comment: index.ts:95 re-exports it as paymentsPublishableKey, and Pulumi.staging.yaml:19 states it is embedded in a client-side widget bundle. A publishable key cannot move money or read objects. Residual, not reported as a leak: prod carries the same sandbox key, which is a payments-configuration question.

ruled_out.assertion: The partner analytics trust policy is an unrestricted wildcard-principal sts:AssumeRole grant
ruled_out.killed_by: pulumi-platform/iam.ts:102 — Condition StringEquals sts:ExternalId. The construct is as wide as it reads; what it applies to is not. The residual concerns ship as the partner over-grant finding and the undefined-configuration finding.

ruled_out.assertion: The /ops/ WAF restriction is bypassable by varying the path's case, since the byte-match has no LOWERCASE transformation
ruled_out.killed_by: pulumi-platform/edge.ts:139 — the ALB listener rule's pathPattern is ['/ops/*'] and ALB path-pattern matching is case-sensitive, so /OPS/x never routes to opsTargetGroup and falls to the 404 fixed-response at edge.ts:87. Both layers are case-sensitive consistently, so no gap opens.

ruled_out.assertion: Non-ASCII in the tenant name reaches a resource name, an IAM path or an ARN unsanitised
ruled_out.killed_by: pulumi-platform/index.ts:33 — a replace of every non-alphanumeric run with '-' on the lowercased, normalised string runs before any use, and index.ts:38 applies it before prefix is built. Every consumer receives the slug, never the raw tenant.

ruled_out.assertion: corporateCidr is a production allow-list value committed in config
ruled_out.killed_by: Both values are RFC 5737 documentation ranges — placeholders, not credentials, and not routable. Their only use is the WAF IpSet referenced under a notStatement in a block rule, so a set matching no real host makes the rule fail closed.

ruled_out.assertion: createLegacyArchive builds a fully public S3 bucket in what ships
ruled_out.killed_by: No call site: a tree-wide grep returns only the definition, and index.ts:45 calls createStorage and nothing else. Pulumi creates no resource for an uncalled function. Reported separately as a latent construct rather than a live exposure.

ruled_out.assertion: Pulumi stack files carry encrypted secret material
ruled_out.killed_by: Neither stack file contains a secure: ciphertext block or an encryptionsalt key. The three real secrets are requireSecret reads at index.ts:20-22 and appear in no tracked file. Negative result, recorded because it is a measurement.

ruled_out.assertion: MODEL_API_KEY defaults to empty, granting unauthenticated access to the model gateway
ruled_out.killed_by: An empty default for an outbound credential makes the gateway call at embedder.py:25 / app.py:87 fail; it does not fail open. No secret present, no authority granted.

ruled_out.assertion: Caller-supplied filters can override the tenancy predicate in the retrieval query
ruled_out.killed_by: atlas-rag/ragsvc/retriever.py:56 — where['tenant_id'] = principal.tenant_id unconditionally overwrites any caller key after where is built from filters, and retriever.py:59 always emits the clause. retriever.py:72 likewise gives the explicit kwargs precedence. Only source_kind becomes an additional clause and its value is bound as a parameter.

ruled_out.assertion: ACL filtering after the SQL query means denied content has already entered the model context
ruled_out.killed_by: atlas-rag/ragsvc/retriever.py:79-81 — the filter runs while hits is being built, and hits is the only thing that leaves search. prompt.render_context iterates that filtered list, so denied content never reaches the context. The filter also fail-closes on an empty or NULL ACL at retriever.py:34.

ruled_out.assertion: /v1/documents lets a tenant write into the shared public collection that every other tenant reads, giving cross-tenant corpus poisoning
ruled_out.killed_by: atlas-rag/ragsvc/retriever.py:56 — the chunk is stored with tenant_id = principal.tenant_id (app.py:185) and the retrieval predicate ANDs tenant_id with the collection clause, so a chunk written by one tenant is invisible to another. The cross-tenant write exists only through /v1/manifest, where the tenant_id itself is forgeable, and is reported there.

ruled_out.assertion: Secrets or business rules are embedded in the assembled system prompt
ruled_out.killed_by: Every line of SYSTEM_INSTRUCTIONS (prompt.py:9-19) was classified: all eleven are public behavioural instructions — a persona, a citation requirement, a refusal rule and tool guidance. No credential, connection string, threshold or customer identifier appears. settings.model_api_key is passed to the client constructor and never to a message.

ruled_out.assertion: http_get can read local files via a file:// URL supplied by the model
ruled_out.killed_by: aiohttp.ClientSession.get accepts http and https only and raises on any other scheme in the declared version. The SSRF finding stands on http(s) to internal hosts; this particular escalation does not.

ruled_out.assertion: The uploads client's followRedirects(true) lets the Authorization header follow a redirect to an arbitrary host
ruled_out.killed_by: atlas-android/app/build.gradle.kts:77 — OkHttp is pinned at 4.12.0, whose RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor removes Authorization when the redirect target fails canReuseConnectionFor. The header set at AttachmentSync.kt:80 does not survive a cross-host hop. A definitive answer would need an instrumented run against a redirecting host, which requires authorization.

ruled_out.assertion: A malicious app registering the atlas:// scheme intercepts a link carrying a credential
ruled_out.killed_by: atlas-android/app/src/main/java/co/atlas/field/ui/DeepLinkRouter.kt:66-93 — the four accepted hosts take a numeric id or no parameter; no token or secret travels in any atlas:// link. Residual: an order id leaks to a squatting app.

ruled_out.assertion: atlas://support lets any app trigger disclosure of the session summary
ruled_out.killed_by: atlas-android/app/src/main/java/co/atlas/field/data/SessionStore.kt:67 — the summary truncates to the last four characters on the path to the sink, and a Toast is not readable cross-app without a granted accessibility service.

ruled_out.assertion: The //-prefixed path in routeWeb's fallback branch overrides the API host
ruled_out.killed_by: Re-read the concatenation: API_BASE + '//evil.example/x' keeps api.fieldops.example as the authority. Only the target branch escapes, and only apiUrl's leading-@ form redirects a host; both are reported separately.

ruled_out.assertion: onReceivedSslError silences TLS errors in the WebView
ruled_out.killed_by: No WebViewClient is set and no onReceivedSslError is overridden anywhere in the file. Recorded as a negative so it is not re-derived; the TLS defect in this component is the permissive trust manager, reported separately.

ruled_out.assertion: A method returning the full session bearer for support tickets is reachable in shipped variants
ruled_out.killed_by: Tree-wide grep returns the definition and nothing else; the only caller of a session summary uses the redacted form. Reported separately as a low-severity latent construct because proguard-rules.pro is absent from the tree, so removal from the artifact could not be established.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection through var("partner_id") into the export's where clause
ruled_out.killed_by: warehouse-dbt/models/exports/partner_extract.sql:16 — the regex substitution removes every character outside [a-z0-9-] before the value reaches the quoted literal, so no quote can survive and the literal cannot be broken out of. The silent coercion that same line performs ships as a separate finding.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection through var("max_rows") into the limit clause
ruled_out.killed_by: warehouse-dbt/models/exports/partner_extract.sql:58 — the int filter coerces to an integer before rendering; a non-numeric value becomes 0. Its uselessness as a bound ships as a separate finding.

ruled_out.assertion: on_schema_change propagates newly-appearing source PII columns into the marts
ruled_out.killed_by: warehouse-dbt/models/marts/customer_pii_masked.sql:21-31 and :40-50 — both branches enumerate their output columns explicitly, so sync_all_columns cannot pull a new source column through; the select * at line 15 is confined to the CTE. Same at stg_payout_events.sql:56-69.

ruled_out.assertion: current_setting('app.tenant_id', true) returning NULL when the setting is absent opens the row-security policy
ruled_out.killed_by: tenant_id = NULL evaluates to NULL, not true, so the policy denies every row. The missing_ok argument fails closed, not open. This looked like a classic bypass and is not one.

ruled_out.assertion: The for-select-only policy leaves INSERT and UPDATE unrestricted on staging and marts
ruled_out.killed_by: warehouse-dbt/macros/row_security.sql:18 — with RLS enabled and no policy matching a command, Postgres denies that command for non-owners. The absence of a write policy is fail-closed, which is why the write grants bite only on exports, where RLS is absent entirely.

ruled_out.assertion: Warehouse credentials are hardcoded in profiles.yml
ruled_out.killed_by: All six credential keys (profiles.yml:12,13,24,25,36,37) are env_var() references with no default, so a missing variable aborts the run. No secret value appears anywhere in the tree.

ruled_out.assertion: Warehouse transport is unprotected or downgradeable
ruled_out.killed_by: warehouse-dbt/profiles.yml:17, :29, :41 — all three targets set sslmode: verify-full, the strongest mode, each paired with an sslrootcert. Checked because it is a common defect in this file type; it is correct here.

ruled_out.assertion: Personal data leaks through the dbt project's logging
ruled_out.killed_by: apply_grants.sql:31 logs a relation name and a role name; row_security.sql:13 logs an adapter type. Neither carries a personal datum, and those are the only two log() calls in the project.

ruled_out.assertion: Text inside the target is addressed to the auditing agent and attempts to change its scope, mode or tooling
ruled_out.killed_by: Swept across all six components: no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .mcp.json, .cursor/rules/ or copilot-instructions file exists anywhere in the tree, and no text instructs a reader to change scope, skip a check or omit a finding. The only non-ASCII characters found are an em-dash in a user-facing string and one in a tenant display name. What is present is unenforced trust assumptions stated as fact in comments, reported as a review hazard rather than as an injection attempt.

findings.title: Request headers accepted as an authenticated identity whenever no bearer token is present, with no proof the request came from the load balancer
findings.class: Authentication bypass by spoofed trusted-proxy header (CWE-290)
findings.evidence: config.ts:28 `trustProxyIdentity: (env.NODE_ENV ?? 'development') === 'production'`. auth.ts:59 `if (!actor && config.trustProxyIdentity) { actor = fromProxyHeaders(c.req.raw.headers); }`. auth.ts:46-51 reads `x-fieldops-actor`, `x-fieldops-org` and `x-fieldops-role`, casting the role with `as Role` and never validating it against the union. `grep -rniE 'hmac|signature|presign' src/` returns no verification of the hop: no mTLS, no shared secret, no source-address check.
findings.impact: A caller reaching the origin directly, or through a load balancer that forwards unknown custom headers (the AWS ALB default), becomes any user of any tenant with any role, unauthenticated. The path is enabled precisely by NODE_ENV=production. Inference not closed: whether the deployed listener strips x-fieldops-* — no LB configuration exists in the tree, and pulumi-platform declares no ECS task definition. What would settle it: the exported listener rule set.
findings.recommendation: Require proof of the hop (mTLS terminated at the app, or an HMAC over the header set keyed to the LB), validate `role` against the Role union, and strip `x-fieldops-*` at the edge. Fail closed when the proof is absent.

triage.reason: No compensating control in the tree; the only layer named is the LB and no artifact for it was supplied.
The values are HTTP request headers, attacker-controlled by definition.
Not debug-gated; it is production-gated at config.ts:28, the inverse.
An ALB rule stripping x-fieldops-* would compensate; no exported LB configuration or task definition arrived. Caps the finding at probable.

scope.established_by: grep for fromProxyHeaders: one definition, one call site, inside requireAuth, which index.ts:28 mounts on /api/v1/*
scope.narrowed_by: fieldops-api/src/config.ts:28 (only when NODE_ENV==='production') and fieldops-api/src/middleware/auth.ts:59 (only when no valid bearer was presented). Not reachable on the /files mount, which uses attachActor.

findings.title: The whole attachments router is mounted a second time behind a middleware that never authenticates, and its tenancy check is written to skip when no caller is known
findings.class: Missing authentication for a critical function; cross-tenant object read (CWE-306, CWE-639)
findings.evidence: index.ts:28-30 mounts the router behind requireAuth on /api/v1/attachments; index.ts:35-36 mounts the same router on config.legacyFilesMount ('/files') behind attachActor, which is auth.ts:74-78 `if (actor && actor.id) c.set('actor', actor); await next();` and never returns 401. The guards are attachments.ts:80 and :97, both `if (actor && actor.orgId !== row.orgId)`. With no credential `actor` is undefined, the `actor &&` short-circuits, and the handler streams the bytes. selectAttachment (attachments.ts:24) queries by id alone with no org predicate. The comment at attachments.ts:78-79 claims 'the grant rides on the link itself'; grep for hmac/signature/presign/createHmac across src/ finds no signature verification anywhere.
findings.impact: GET /files/<id>/raw with no credential at all returns the attachment bytes of any tenant — work-order evidence photographed by field technicians at customer sites. Same defect on /files/<id> for metadata.
findings.recommendation: Mount the legacy prefix behind requireAuth, or implement and verify the pre-signed grant before the handler; make the tenancy comparison unconditional (`if (!actor || actor.orgId !== row.orgId) return 403`) and add the org predicate to selectAttachment.

triage.reason: attachActor (auth.ts:74-78) is the only middleware on that prefix and calls next() unconditionally; requireAuth matches /api/v1/* only.
legacyFilesMount is a hardcoded constant at config.ts:32; index.ts:35-36 register unconditionally.
The exposure is intended per the comment at index.ts:33-34 but nothing bounds it; the bound the comment names is not implemented anywhere in the tree.
Both internet->API and tenant<->tenant boundaries are crossed.
Attachments carry customer-site evidence uploaded by technicians.
The construct applies to more than it reads, not less: one app.route line re-exposes three handlers.

scope.established_by: joined the app.use/app.route registrations in index.ts against the handler list in attachments.ts, then traced c.get('actor') back to the two middlewares
scope.narrowed_by: fieldops-api/src/index.ts:28 — under /api/v1/attachments/* requireAuth guarantees a non-null actor, so the same two lines behave correctly on that mount. The defect is the second mount.

findings.title: JWT signing key has a hardcoded fallback and nothing fails the boot when the environment variable is missing
findings.class: Use of hard-coded credential; missing fail-closed initialization (CWE-798)
findings.evidence: config.ts:23 `sessionSecret: env.SESSION_SECRET ?? 'local-development-session-key'`. Consumed at auth.ts:20 and session.ts:9 by `new TextEncoder().encode(config.sessionSecret)`, which both signs (session.ts:55 `.sign(secret)`) and verifies (auth.ts:26 `jwtVerify(...)`). `grep -rnE 'throw |assert|process.exit' src/` returns no hit: there is no startup validation anywhere in the service.
findings.impact: A deployment that omits SESSION_SECRET boots successfully and signs every session token with a string published in the source tree. Anyone with the repository mints a token for any sub, org, role and crews (session.ts:49-51) — full impersonation of any tenant and role. The failure is silent: no log line, no health signal, no boot failure distinguishes it from a correct deployment. Inference not closed: whether production sets the variable; config.ts:3-5 asserts the deployed stacks override it and no task definition exists in this tree to confirm.
findings.recommendation: Remove the fallback; throw at module load when SESSION_SECRET is absent or shorter than 32 bytes. Treat the published string as compromised and rotate.

triage.reason: No layer validates configuration; the grep for throw/assert/exit over src/ is exhaustive and empty.
The defect is not that an attacker supplies the key but that a key everyone can read becomes the signing key by default.
config.ts:3-5 claims deployed stacks override it through the task-definition environment; no task definition arrived, and pulumi-platform defines none. Caps the finding at probable.
`??` is exactly what it reads as.

scope.established_by: grep for sessionSecret and SESSION_SECRET across all six components: one declaration, two consumers

findings.title: Work-order list cache key omits the crew filter that decides which rows the caller may see
findings.class: Caching of a private response under a key missing the authorization dimension (CWE-524)
findings.evidence: cache.ts:11-12 `listKey(orgId, status, page)` returns `wo:list:${orgId}:${status}:${page}`. workorders.ts:53-55 builds that key, reads the cache and returns the hit before any narrowing. The narrowing is applied afterwards at workorders.ts:60 `const crews = visibleCrewFilter(actor)` and :67-69 `sql += ' and crew_id = any(...)'`. policy.ts:48-49: a tech gets actor.crewIds, everyone else gets null (the whole org). `limit` is likewise absent from the key.
findings.impact: Within one org, whoever misses the cache first populates it for everyone else for listCacheTtlSeconds (45s, config.ts:38). A manager's request caches the whole org board and the next tech request in that window is served it — work orders for crews the tech is not on, with notes and assignedTo. The reverse direction truncates a manager's board. A ?limit=1 request caches a one-row payload for every subsequent caller. The x-cache header at workorders.ts:56 makes the collision observable.
findings.recommendation: Include the authorization dimension in the key — visibleCrewFilter(actor), sorted or null, plus limit — or cache the unnarrowed rows and apply the filter after the cache read.

triage.reason: The cache read at workorders.ts:55 returns before line 60; no layer re-filters the payload.
Two principals inside one org; visibleCrewFilter exists precisely because they are meant to see different rows.
The payload is work orders with notes and assignedTo.
Nothing narrows it: the key is identical for every role.

scope.established_by: grep for listKey/cache.get/cache.set across src/: one reader, one writer
scope.narrowed_by: fieldops-api/src/lib/cache.ts:12 — the key does include orgId, so the collision is bounded to within one tenant and is not a cross-tenant leak.

findings.title: Brute-force limiter covers /session/login while /session/token performs the identical credential check unlimited
findings.class: Missing rate limiting on an authentication endpoint — unguarded sibling (CWE-307)
findings.evidence: index.ts:24 `app.use('/api/v1/session/login', loginLimiter)` — an exact path, one route. session.ts:67 and session.ts:92 both reach the identical `findPrincipal` + `passwordMatches` pair, and session.ts:95 returns a usable token. `grep -rn 'loginLimiter|rateLimit('` gives one instantiation (rateLimit.ts:43) and one registration (index.ts:24). The session routes are public because app.route('/api/v1/session', ...) at index.ts:25 is registered before app.use('/api/v1/*', requireAuth) at index.ts:28.
findings.impact: POST /api/v1/session/token with grantType=password reaches the same credential check with no limiter, from an unauthenticated caller: the 8-attempts-per-minute guard (config.ts:40) is bypassed by changing one path segment. /recover (session.ts:111) is likewise uncovered.
findings.recommendation: Attach the limiter to the router (session.use('*', loginLimiter)) rather than to one path in index.ts, and key it by submitted identity as well as by client address. Make the public exemption explicit rather than a consequence of registration order.

triage.reason: The grep shows exactly one limiter registration and it names one path.
/token is registered unconditionally at session.ts:84.
app.use(path, mw) with a non-wildcard path cannot match a different final segment.

A WAF or ALB rule could rate-limit at the edge; no such artifact arrived. It would apply equally to /login, whose in-app limiter shows the project does not rely on it — but the answer is UNKNOWN, so the finding does not ship as confirmed.

scope.established_by: joined the middleware registrations in index.ts against the four handlers in session.ts (/login, /token, /recover, /catalog)
scope.narrowed_by: fieldops-api/src/index.ts:24 — /login alone is covered; /catalog needs no coverage.

findings.title: Work-order notes interpolated into HTML unescaped, behind a blacklist sanitizer that reconstructs the tag it removes
findings.class: Stored cross-site scripting; sanitizer that cannot reject (CWE-79, CWE-184)
findings.evidence:
workorders.ts:197 `
${wo.notes}
` — the one interpolation in the template that is not wrapped in escapeHtml, while lines 189, 192, 194 and 195 are. The only control is policy.ts:58-62, which removes complete pairs,
findings.impact: An authenticated tech writes notes via POST or PATCH; any dispatcher or manager opening /api/v1/workorders/<id>/print executes the payload in the origin's context with their own session.
findings.recommendation: Escape at the sink — escapeHtml(wo.notes) — and if rich text is required replace scrubNotes with an allowlist sanitizer applied at render. Add a CSP with a nonce to the print response.

notes is a request body field constrained only in length (z.string().max(8000)).
The sink is c.html() at workorders.ts:200: the string is served as text/html.
There is no server-side equivalent making this defence in depth; it is the only control on the path.

scope.established_by: enumerated every ${...} in the template literal at workorders.ts:188-198 and split them by whether escapeHtml wraps them
scope.narrowed_by: fieldops-api/src/routes/workorders.ts:181 — the sink is skipped when format=json.

findings.title: Default print template renders wo.title unescaped through a compiled function, two lines above the escaped copy of the same value
findings.class: Stored cross-site scripting (CWE-79)
findings.evidence:
